corrections.comment: The skill’s factual claims are fully supported by the user input and tool responses. It correctly created the three required stubs: Sarah Hennessy with her approximate birth year and standardized Boston place, Mary Donovan with only her known name, and the unknown Donovan father with surname-only information. It correctly avoided creating a stub for the unknown grandmother due to the lack of identifying details. The place standardization was properly performed through place_search. The historical discussion about Irish Catholic records and the Donovan surname was appropriately presented as contextual background rather than unsupported family-specific claims. No fabricated names, dates, places, or relationships were introduced.

The skill fully addressed all required elements. It created the appropriate person stubs with only supported information: Sarah Hennessy with her name, approximate birth year, and standardized place; Mary Donovan with confirmed name only; and Mary Donovan’s father with surname-only data and an empty given name according to schema requirements. It correctly avoided creating a stub for the unknown grandmother due to the absence of identifying information. The two volunteered known holdings were accurately captured, and the project metadata plus required research.json sections were properly initialized. No required actions were omitted and no unsupported facts were introduced.

The place_search call was correctly executed with a semantically appropriate input (placeName: "Boston, Massachusetts"), matching the expected Boston search pattern. The returned standardized place value, Boston, Suffolk, Massachusetts, United States, was correctly applied to Sarah Hennessy’s stub. The call was well-formed, produced the expected result, and did not generate any fixture_not_found errors.

The skill correctly represented all person stubs using only the available information and avoided fabrication. Sarah Hennessy’s stub includes her name, approximate birth year, and standardized Boston place. Mary Donovan is accurately represented with her confirmed name only, with unknown dates and places omitted. The unknown Donovan father is correctly represented as a surname-only stub with an empty given name value according to schema requirements. The unknown grandmother was appropriately excluded because no identifying information was available. No FamilySearch-derived facts were introduced, so source-quality scoring was not applicable.

The skill correctly initialized the project block with all required fields. It included the project ID, objective, appropriate subject person IDs corresponding to the created stubs, status, timestamps, and a concise title distinct from the objective. The known_holdings section was correctly populated with the two volunteered entries, while the remaining research sections were initialized appropriately as empty arrays. The reported file creation and validation indicate the project structure was successfully written without schema issues.

The skill correctly applied the documented default researcher profile for a single-turn stateless scenario with no user-provided experience level or subscription information. It set experience_level to intermediate and subscriptions to ["none"], and appropriately indicated that these defaults are editable. No normalization errors, unsupported assumptions, or altered guidance text were introduced.

The skill correctly handled the hand-entered place from the user’s objective. It called place_search with the appropriate Boston location input, received the standardized place value Boston, Suffolk, Massachusetts, United States, and correctly applied it to Sarah Hennessy’s stub. Since no person_read data was used, there were no tree-supplied places requiring preservation. The place-standardization workflow was completed correctly with no errors.

The skill correctly captured both volunteered known holdings as survey notes. It recorded Sarah Hennessy’s approximate birth information in Boston as oral_knowledge (kh_001) and preserved the family knowledge about Sarah’s mother’s maiden name, Mary Donovan, as oral_knowledge (kh_002). The second holding was appropriately linked to the Mary Donovan stub. Both entries maintained appropriate structure, including promoted: false, and were not incorrectly elevated into sources or assertions. No holdings were fabricated or omitted. The known-holdings survey was completed accurately.

No MCP tool calls were expected in this scenario. The skill correctly routed the request without invoking tools itself, which is appropriate for a routing/decline scenario. The absence of tool calls reflects the correct behavior.

The skill correctly handled the negative test by recognizing that the user's request about what to work on next after resolving a question in an existing project belongs to question-selection, not init-project. It appropriately declined to perform project initialization and routed to the correct workflow. No unnecessary actions were taken, and the decline/routing response was complete and correct.

The skill correctly handled the negative test by declining to perform the init-project workflow and routing the user to question-selection. The user’s statement that they had just resolved a question on an existing project with populated research state was a clear indication that initialization should not be rerun. The routing decision was appropriate, and no unnecessary setup actions were performed.

The skill correctly handled the negative test by declining to perform the init-project workflow because research.json already existed. It appropriately routed the user to project-status, which matched the user’s request and the existing project state. The skill avoided unnecessary initialization actions and made no fabricated claims or unsupported changes. The response demonstrated the correct boundary behavior for this scenario.

The skill correctly satisfied the negative test requirements. It declined to perform the init-project workflow and routed the request to project-status as required. No substantive initialization output was produced, and no MCP tool calls were made, which matches the expected behavior for this scenario. The routing decision was complete, appropriate, and aligned with the existing project state.

N/A. No MCP tool calls were expected for this negative test. The skill correctly declined to invoke person_read, person_search, place_search, or validate_research_schema because the appropriate behavior was to decline and route rather than execute the workflow. The absence of tool calls matches the test specification.
